placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_lasalle, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is NOT a measurement of this frontage either: it is the line the buildings already standing on this face were built to, adopted so that the face carries one street wall rather than two (T-0104). The plat module's lot margin still fixes the side lines this run stands clear of; what it does not fix is a street line that other records had already set, and its west wall is fixed by the east wall of recon_1835_blk_south_water_lasalle_f2_10, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

persons.name: Hiram Pearsons
persons.note: Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. It gives a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, and it is a retrospective of 1884: a YEAR off it is documented, a MONTH is not, and it says nothing whatever about 1835. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Pearsons, Hiram” (poll_1834_087, line 256). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Pearsons' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. lot 6 of block 141 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 1877.02 acres stated in all, for $40296.00 (ls0012, ls0013, ls0301, ls0302, ls0303, ls0304, ls0305, ls0306, ls0307, ls0308, ls0309, ls0310, ls0311, ls0312, ls0313, ls0314, ls0315, ls0316, ls0317, ls0318, ls0664, ls0665, ls0666, ls0671, ls0748, ls0753, ls0754, ls0818, ls1407, ls0742, ls0747, ls0772, ls0781, ls0782, ls0783, ls0784, ls0785, ls0786, ls0787, ls0802, ls0803, ls0804, ls0805, ls0835, ls0843, ls0844, ls1406, ls1402, ls1403, ls1404, ls1405). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS COOK, UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $33010.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. The register states this purchaser's residence as COOK, so the sale is contemporary evidence that a man of this name lived in Cook County on the date of sale. It is not evidence that he lived in the town. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: PEARSONS HIRAM matches Hiram Pearsons: the forename names Hiram Pearsons of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

The surname is spelled both Pearson and Pearsons within two pages of each other and this record uses the form on the incorporation poll. THE OCCUPATION IS THE WEAKEST FIELD HERE and is graded documented only because the office-holding is; a source that names his business should replace it.

frontage.why: T-0429, and the ground it stands on was unblocked by an owner's ruling rather than found. T-0143 and T-0188 each refused to tighten a party-line row against a street line that might move, and T-0317 inherited the refusal; T-0009 closed it on 2026-08-29 under the owner's ruling that THE DRAWN SOUTH WATER LINE DOES NOT MOVE — the corridor was re-derived from committed control and data/streets/1835.json was not touched. That refusal is what had held this reach, and it is discharged. THE FACE IS THE BLOCK'S OWN, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: tools/measure_street_frontage.py reads South Water and Lake as the two faces of this block, the committed street hierarchy in data/streets/1835.json grades both `principal`, and South Water is the river street the owner's reference plate draws — 'South Water Street in 1834', roughly ten one-storey log and frame buildings shoulder to shoulder facing the river. This run is the west half of that row on this block. THE LINE IS NOT AUTHORED AT ALL, which is the difference between this run and the first deal's: the face is already built, so the run declares `adopts_face_line` and the 1.5 m is MEASURED off the three units the first deal stands on the same face — 1.4998, 1.4996 and 1.5004 m, a 0.8 mm spread — under T-0104's clause. A street wall is one wall, and this row joins one rather than opening one. THE CORNER CLAUSE BINDS AND THE FABRIC RULE AGREES WITH IT, which is the parcel's one new reading. Lot 0 is the block's free CORNER lot, at South Water and LaSalle, and the core density standard's third clause says a corner lot BUILDS TO THE CORNER: the run is anchored WEST, 1.5 m clear of the corner margin, and chains east on shared party walls. The frontage-fabric rule (T-0022) independently says a log dwelling takes the WEST END of a principal-street row where the block was dealt one, and this block was dealt a D1. On blk_randolph_market (T-0317) the corner clause and the end rule pointed in opposite directions and the parcel had to choose; here the corner clause and the fabric rule name the SAME unit, so the log cabin takes the corner and nothing has to be traded away. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the strip's two ends and the party walls between units are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the lots this run was dealt are named here so the ledger can count them rather than shared out one per unit.
